newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parliament scraps compulsory currency swap.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parliament scraps compulsory currency swap.

text.p: Ukrainian central bank believes parliament's decision to scrap a law requiring companies to change 50 percent of their export revenues for hryvnias would have a limited impact on the economy.

"In reality exporters sell about 80 percent of their hard currency. Therefore we do not think that repealing the requirement would mean significantly less hard currency being sold on the market," Serhiy Yaremenko, head of foreign currency department, said.
The new rule, passed by parliament late on Tuesday, requires the signature of President Leonid Kuchma before it takes effect and this is expected around the end of the month.
The International Monetary Fund had made the repeal of the rule one of the conditions for Ukraine to receive a three-year Extended Fund Facility.
Buying and selling of hard currency and hryvnias takes place on the Ukrainian Interbank Currency Exchange, where the hryvnia's level is set daily.
Yaremenko said most businesses actively sell hard currency to pay their bills in Ukraine, where most transactions are conducted in the national hryvnia currency.
Prior to the law being repealed exporters were required to sell their hard currency within five days of a transaction's completion.
The $2.5 to $3 billion IMF loan may be delivered next month, once Ukraine approves the 1997 budget which has been delayed due to bickering between the government and parliament.
